Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Coldfall Primary School. We are a large, vibrant three-form entry primary school located in Muswell Hill, North London.
Coldfall Primary is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all of its pupils. All pupils will choose their Coldfall 'Give Me 5' adults who they can talk to.
We aim to give each child the best foundations for them to be happy, confident and successful lifelong learners. Our stimulating curriculum reflects and embraces the diverse culture and backgrounds of our community. We are committed to ensuring that children master the fundamentals of reading, writing and mathematics, as well as ensuring the broad and exciting curriculum enables each child the opportunity to find their passion and develop their talents.

Latest Social News
Year 3 had a wonderful day with artist Julie Vermeille from the Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration @qbcentre , creating their own illustrations using pastels, watercolour and collage. Look at these fabulous creations, inspired by the work of Jon Klassen.
Year 5 had an amazing day exploring Epping Forest! From exploring woodland, grassland and aquatic habitats to pond dipping, the children discovered nature up close while enjoying the glorious sunshine. A fantastic day of outdoor learning, adventure and smiles all round!
Haringey Primary School Sport Shield winners 2nd year in a row (only been running for 2 years!), after winning 13 school sport competitions this academic year.
Pelican Class had an amazing time at Tolmers! We loved taking part in archery, Aero Ball, orienteering, pedal carts and tackling the vertical wall. We ended the day with a lovely campfire, toasting marshmallows and making unforgettable memories.
We loved having Ms Colquhoun's nephew, Euan Murray visit us today. He is a para-athlete who runs the T64 100m and 200m sprint. Look out Brisbane Paralympics 2032!
Year 5 rounded off Sports Week with some tennis fun in the beautiful sunshine. All that was missing was strawberries and cream!
A huge thank you to Mr Browning for organising yet another fun-filled activity for Year 5! American football was a big hit, and everyone had a fantastic time. Thank you for creating such memorable experiences!
We were so lucky to have our wonderful parent helpers, Fay and Sarah, come in to carry out a fantastic art lesson with Pelican Class! They planned and guided us in creating these beautiful portraits, and we had such a lovely afternoon getting creative.
From dancing feet, volley ball, yoga to wheelchair basketball and rounders, Year 4 have been having so much fun adding to the school 10,000 hours sports week.
Year 5 had a fantastic time during their one-hour skateboarding session as part of Coldfall's Sport Week! Great fun, lots of new skills, and plenty of smiles.
Boxing Inspiration for Year 5! Our Year 5 pupils were treated to an incredible afternoon with professional boxers Mitchell Asare and Cameron McKay, who wowed everyone with a fantastic boxing display and shared what it takes to succeed. Miss Queeney also welcomed back former pupil and her mum, Laura Saperstein – former professional boxer and now boxing wear designer – who spoke about the power of discipline, perseverance and self-belief. An inspiring session showing our children that hard work, resilience and believing in yourself can take you anywhere!
A little bit of everything, all at once! This is what lunchtime looks like with OPAL. Tunnels for the explorers. Sandpit for the builders. Lego for the creators. Painting for the artists. Just pure, child-led joy. Swipe through to see our busy bees in action!

Head Teacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Coldfall Primary School. We are a large, vibrant three-form entry primary school located in Muswell Hill, North London.
Coldfall Primary is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all of its pupils. All pupils will choose their Coldfall 'Give Me 5' adults who they can talk to.
We aim to give each child the best foundations for them to be happy, confident and successful lifelong learners. Our stimulating curriculum reflects and embraces the diverse culture and backgrounds of our community. We are committed to ensuring that children master the fundamentals of reading, writing and mathematics, as well as ensuring the broad and exciting curriculum enables each child the opportunity to find their passion and develop their talents.
We employ enthusiastic, passionate, vocational teachers who recognise the imperative upon them to be exemplary role models and to nurture each child to become the best that they can be. The school is committed to developing the practice of the teachers to be exemplary so that they can have the greatest impact on the children they serve.
Coldfall is fortunate to have an extensive and beautiful outdoor space, supported by specialist teachers, that provides unrivalled opportunities to develop a healthy, active lifestyle and also to learn how to care for our environment and its importance. Everything we do at Coldfall is rooted in a values-based approach that builds moral, responsible and active global citizens who develop, value and maintain positive relationships with all.
Thank you for visiting our website. Navigate the pages to discover more about our wonderful school. Click HERE to find out how to book a tour of our school.
Head Teacher’s Welcome

Governors
The Role of a School Governor at Coldfall Primary School
The governing body is responsible for the long-term strategic direction of the school. It has statutory responsibilities including agreeing the school budget and expenditure and ensuring key policies are in place. Governors do not get involved in the day-to-day running of the school. The role is one of ‘critical friend’, asking questions and providing challenge and support in any areas in which they have expertise. Governor training is provided – new governors can attend training sessions at Haringey’s Professional Development Centre (usually timetabled to allow for people who work full-time) and the school also arranges training sessions in school, usually held before meetings.
Governors’ terms of office are expected to be four years. They meet twice a term – once every six weeks for the full governing body meetings, usually held on Thursday evenings at 5.00pm in school. These meetings can run until about 8.00pm. Governors are also required to join one of three separate committees, Finance and Site (F&S), Human Resources (HR) or Teaching and Learning. These committees usually meet mid-week at 8.00am in school, once every half-term. The lead governor of each committee prepares the minutes and submits them to the clerk for distribution to the full governing body.
We also have ‘link’ governors with areas of specific interest linked to the School Development Plan.
The minutes of governing body meetings can be found on this page.
If you would like to contact the Clerk of the Governors you can email Maria Fletcher.
If you would like to file a complaint with the governing body, please email Nia Harding-Rickards for further assistance.

Green School
We are an Eco School
Coldfall Primary is an eco-friendly school, and strives to improve every year. We teach children to be environmentally responsible, and to be activists and upstanders in line with the school’s Golden Threads. Our aim is for children to grow up understanding their responsibility towards each other and our environment. Children are the future generation: they are the future leaders and citizens of our planet. It is therefore vital that they develop an appreciation for the Earth and a desire to protect it. In order to achieve this, the school incorporates ‘green’ teaching and learning activities into its everyday practice and lessons are regularly conducted outside.
Green School
Children in Nursery, Reception, Year 1, Year 3 and Year 4 have regular Green School lessons with our Green/Sustainability teacher, Mrs Greene. These provide space in the curriculum for children to connect with and learn about nature in an enjoyable and creative way. The lessons also help build children’s wellbeing and resilience. Lessons take place outdoors, usually on the school’s nature trail (a wooded area of the school grounds that is part of Coldfall Woods) or on our school allotment. Reception children visit Coldfall Woods. The children learn to use tools, tie knots and identify local birds, other animals and plants. Every year, they sow, harvest and eat fruits or vegetables that they have grown themselves. At the end of their time at Coldfall, they will have a thorough understanding of what it means to live sustainably and specific actions we can take to help our planet. Children need wellies in school for their Green School lessons.

Star Squad
Whole school eco initiatives are led by our Star Squad, an eco-committee with a representative from each class from Year 1 to Year 6. Working with our Green/Sustainability teacher, they set the school’s green agenda for the year and coordinate whole school green initiatives and events throughout the year, such as the Great Big School Clean (cleaning up litter) and Switch Off Fortnight (saving energy). They monitor the results and report back to their classes. In 2024-2025 we are focused on Litter, Energy and Water. In addition to all of the hard work that the Star Squad does, each class has eco-monitors who help with the recycling and remind their peers and teachers to switch off the lights when they are not needed. Children are made aware of the value of paper and are encouraged to ensure all paper is used carefully and fully.
Green Flag
In 2008, Coldfall Primary became the first Haringey school to be awarded a prestigious Green Flag by the Eco-Schools Programme for our work with children on sustainable development and living. We have renewed this every year since then and in June 2023 we were awarded a Green Flag with distinction – recognition of our ongoing efforts to work with our school community and other partners on environmental issues. Our work was featured on ITV London’s evening news programme on January 16th 2023, when they came to film our nursery children taking part in the RSPB’s Big Schools’ Birdwatch. In addition to Green School lessons and whole school eco initiatives, topics such as conservation, biodiversity and climate change are woven into the school curriculum in every year group.
Eco Code
Star Squad revised our school Eco Code in 2024 to reflect our current aims. This is displayed around school and staff, children and families are asked to follow it.
Travel to School
Coldfall promotes safe and active travel to school as this is good for us and good for the planet. We have achieved Gold Level accreditation from Transport for London’s community project Stars, aimed at promoting safe and active travel to and from school. Our Year 5 Junior Travel Ambassadors (JTAs) play a key role in this, working with our Green/Sustainability teacher to promote safe and active travel throughout the year. The JTAs monitor traffic and road safety around the school entrances every week, and communicate with families and children to pass on important messages about safety - for example, reminding children on bikes to wear a helmet, and younger children to hold an adult’s hand when crossing the road.
We take part in Walk to School Month and Walk to School Week every year, and campaign to reduce cars around the school entrances and stop drivers from stopping on the zigzags.
School Street
In April 2021, Coldfall Avenue became a School Street following a campaign by our Star Squad to improve road safety near the school. A School Street is a walking and cycling zone that operates during peak drop-off and pick-up times outside a school. Only people walking and cycling and those with vehicle permits are eligible to enter the zone. Our School Street operates on Coldfall Avenue N10 from 8.00-9.30am and 2.30-4.00pm, Monday to Friday during term time only. The scheme has really improved safety near the Coldfall Avenue school entrance.
Walk to School Week and 10-Minute Walk Zone
We promote walking to school and we have a ’10-minute walk zone’ map in our playground, showing the area in which children can walk to school in 10 minutes or less. The aim of this zone is to encourage as many families as possible to walk either all or part of the way to school. If you do need to drive, please try to park outside of the ‘10-minute walk zone’ and walk the rest of the way. Remember that walking to school is one of the easiest ways to improve your family’s health and wellbeing. You will also be helping to improve congestion and air quality around the school entrances, making it much safer for children as they approach the school gates. Best of all, it’s free! We encourage everyone to walk a little each day even if they are driven part of the way.
Lunches and Food Waste
Our school lunch menu is very healthy and Monday is a meat-free day. A fresh self-service salad bar is available every day. We try to reduce food waste at Coldfall and have food waste bins in the dining hall which are collected by the Council for composting. We also encourage children who bring food from home to use reusable containers instead of plastic bags and cling film. Our ultimate goal is to have waste-free lunches. In addition, we have a three-bin composting system in our allotment which encourages children to recycle organic waste from their morning snacks. We grow a range of fruit and vegetables in our allotment for use in our food technology room. Learning about cooking is one of the children’s favourite activities and it is particularly rewarding when they get to sample produce that they have helped to grow.
Other Green Initiatives
The school has solar panels installed to help reduce its energy consumption and has introduced a range of other energy-saving measures. We even have an eco-friendly school uniform. It is made from 100% pure organic cotton, is eco-friendly (no nasty chemicals are used in its production) and ethically and sustainably produced in socially compliant factories certified by GOTS (Global Organic Textile Standards). We welcome families’ support in developing our green agenda.
Green News
In April 2024, our Year 5 Junior Travel Ambassadors took part in Junior Road Watch with the Met Police. This project aims to raise awareness of the dangers of speeding. The children got to use a speed gun on roads near school and talk to drivers who were driving too fast after the police had pulled them over. They thoroughly enjoyed it and learnt a lot about road safety, which they will pass on to their friends and families.

Premises Hire
Some areas of the school are available for private hire outside of school hours. We have a large multi-function hall suitable for parties, conferences and meetings. The playing fields and the multi-use games area can also be hired. We do not hire out the premises for adult parties.
After reading our Premises Hire Policy below, please submit the form below to request hire of the premises, and we will get back to you as soon as possible.
Coldfall Main Hall
The main hall at Coldfall is a self-contained extension of the school building. The outdoor facilities of the school grounds and the amenities inside the hall together offer a wide range of possibilities. There is an outdoor decking area with stunning views over Coldfall Woods. There are multiple power points, self-contained toilet facilities and disabled access throughout. There is access to a serving area for light refreshments.
The hall can seat approximately 200 people and is ideal for meetings and conferences. The flooring is wooden laminate and suitable for activities such as exercise or self-defence classes. Excellent acoustics and the size of the hall make it particularly suitable for music performances, drama and dance.
Coldfall Lower Hall
Coldfall’s smaller lower hall has a capacity of 100 people and can also be used for sport and keep fit, meetings, conferences and children’s parties. There is a separate entrance, toilets and disabled access.
MUGA
The multi-use games area (MUGA) is an outdoor astro-turf games facility located off the main field. It has nets for ball games, and is self-contained.
School Field
The expansive playing field of the school is a vast outdoor area, ideally suited for hosting a myriad of events and activities.
Security, Supervision and Support
The Site Manager or a representative of the school will be present whenever the halls are in use and will ensure that all functions and meetings are conducted within the rules agreed by the hirer, as well as providing help and advice if required.

Autumn 2026 Club Descriptions
American Football (Years 3-6)
XL Performance offers exciting after-school American football sessions with a focus on inclusion and fun. The sessions welcome pupils of all skill levels and help children develop teamwork, confidence and key athletic skills in a supportive environment.
Animation and Filmmaking Club (Years 5-6)
Join our club for all things stop-motion animation and filmmaking. Children will learn how to create animated films in 2D and 3D using tablet apps, and will also devise and shoot live-action films as part of a crew. The club is ideal for children who enjoy art, IT, creative writing, cameras and editing. Films are shared with parents and carers at the end of term. No experience is necessary. The course is run by Lucy Whitehead from Animating Education: www.animatingeducation.co.uk
Art Club (Years 3-4 and Years 4-6)
Art Club is delivered by Sam Starr, an experienced art teacher who believes in building confidence and ownership in young artists. Children will learn about art and culture, explore different ways of working, and celebrate and play with lots of creative ideas. www.thestarryartroom.co.uk
Arts and Crafts Club (Years 1-3 and Years 3-6)
Arts and Crafts is taught by Mrs Danisi. Children will use a range of materials and techniques to create varied pieces of art in a relaxed, creative setting.
Athletics (Years 3-6)
These sessions are led by Mr Browning, our PE teacher. Athletics Club will focus on speed, fitness and general athletic skills, helping children build confidence and improve technique.
Basketball (Years 4-6)
Basketball Club is led by one of our teaching assistants. The club covers all aspects of the game and aims to develop each child’s individual skill set through drills, teamwork and game play.
Capoeira Club London (Years 3-6)
Capoeira Club London coaches prepare classes that develop concentration, co-ordination and confidence in a fun and friendly environment. This distinctive art form teaches acrobatic skills, supports balance and core strength, and helps children develop social skills. Participants also learn to sing and count in Portuguese. All coaches are insured, first-aid trained and DBS checked. www.capoeiraclub.co.uk
Chess (Years 3-6)
Chess is delivered by Kamlesh Karia. Children taught by Kamlesh have taken part in local and national competitions, winning trophies and gaining valuable experience of competing with others. Chess continues to be a popular activity at Coldfall.
Cooking Club with Rookie Cooks (Years 4-6)
Booking for this club is directly via Rookie Cooks and not via Arbor. Please book via www.rookiecooks.com. Children will cook a range of sweet and savoury dishes during the Autumn term. They will learn to follow recipes, weigh ingredients accurately, chop and prepare food safely, and work sensibly around kitchen equipment. Cooking also encourages creativity, teamwork, confidence and a willingness to try new foods.
Cricket Club (Years 3-6)
This club is run by James from Middlesex Cricket. Children will learn and practise the skills needed to improve in cricket, using specialist drills alongside fun and varied games.
Cross Country, Long-Distance Running and Conditioning (Years 3-6)
This club is for children who have an interest in running and would like to improve their stamina and confidence over longer distances. Sessions will include relaxed runs, interval training and conditioning exercises to help children look after their muscles.
Dance (Years 1-2 and Years 1-6)
J.K. Dance Academy, founded by Jessica Hewitson in 2003, is an independent dance school in North London. J.K. Dance provides an inclusive, kind and exciting environment for pupils of all abilities. Children will learn elements of modern, street, stage and freestyle dance, helping their confidence, skill and enjoyment of dance to grow. www.jkdanceacademy.co.uk
Dodgeball (Years 3-4 and Years 5-6)
Dodgeball is led by Mr Hylton, our PE assistant. The club includes a range of dodgeball variations and teaches the specific skills needed to play the game safely, confidently and as part of a team.
Drama Club (Years 1-2)
Drama Club is run by Debutots and offers a blend of interactive storytelling and dramatic play. Sessions are designed to build self-confidence, encourage self-expression and nurture a love of language and story. Each week, original interactive stories transport children to an imaginary world where they become the characters, sounds and scenery of the tales. https://debutots.co.uk/finchley-hampstead-muswellhill/
Girls’ Football (Years 1-2 and Years 3-6)
Girls’ Football is run by Mr Hylton, our PE assistant. Sessions focus on skill development and small-sided games, covering the fundamentals of the game while developing confidence, teamwork and individual skill.
Gymnastics (Years 1-2) with Juliette Tive-Hive
Juliette and Marcy provide after-school gymnastics sessions in partnership with Coldfall Primary. They have 20 years’ experience teaching gymnastics and dance in North London across general gymnastics, acro, cheer, pre-school and display gymnastics. With a strong focus on floor agility, children will explore and develop gymnastic technique in a fun and motivational space. Juliette also runs a community session from 4.45pm to 5.45pm on Wednesday afternoons for school Years 2-6. For more information and bookings, email Juliette at jthsport@gmail.com
Gymnastics (Years 3-6) with Kingfisher Gymnastics Club
Kingfisher Gymnastics Club is a long-established club, registered with British Gymnastics and London Gymnastics. The coaches are experienced and qualified, and staff hold current DBS and safeguarding certificates. Classes follow the British Gymnastics Proficiency Awards and focus on strength, flexibility, co-ordination and confidence. Children work on floor, table vault, springboards, beams and bars, with support tailored to individual needs.
Hockey (Years 3-6)
Hockey is led by coaches from Southgate Hockey Club. Sessions focus on the fundamentals of the game, increasing skill and confidence while helping children master control using a hockey stick.
Lego Club (Years 1-6)
Lego Club is run by Miss Amoako and Mrs Lau, two of our teaching assistants. Children will develop fine motor skills, problem-solving and imagination by using Lego to build creations linked to a theme set by the leader.
Minecraft Club (Years 1-6)
Minecraft Club is delivered by Mrs Orford. Children work together to build a shared world and practise online communication and problem-solving skills in a safe, contained environment. The focus is on the collaborative, creative and social benefits of Minecraft and the joy of imaginative play.
Mixed Football (Years 1-2, Years 3-4 and Years 5-6)
Football clubs are delivered by Global Football Academy. Groups are mixed and divided according to year group. Sessions use small-sided games to develop teamwork and skills, with an emphasis on all children being active participants throughout.
Mixed Table Tennis (Years 4-6)
These sessions are led by Mr Browning, our PE teacher, with support from former Coldfall pupils. Table tennis focuses on playing the game through friendly competition to build confidence and develop skills.
Multi-Sports (Years 1-2 and Years 3-6)
Multi-Sports is led by Mr Hylton, our PE assistant, and other members of the school team where scheduled. Children will play a range of sports and learn the specific skills needed to participate. Sessions focus on skill development, teamwork and small-sided games.
Skateboarding (Years 3-6)
No experience is needed—just turn up in trainers and get ready to roll! North London Skate Club provides all the equipment, including skateboards, helmets, protective pads, and ramps. Their DBS-checked and first-aid-trained instructors support every ability level, from complete beginners to confident skaters. Each session is structured, safe, and designed to help children stay active, build confidence, develop new skills, and have fun on four wheels.
Children should bring a water bottle and wear comfortable clothes and trainers.
Yoga and Mindfulness (Years 1-3)
Yoga and Mindfulness provides children with time to pause and become more aware of their breathing, body and emotions. Sessions support relaxation, flexibility, co-ordination and strength through breathing and stretching exercises, yoga poses, stories, mindful activities and colouring.
